prompt: Create a scientific overview diagram for an explanatory article on Machine Learning for Robotics, white background, thin rounded outlines, restrained pastel blue purple orange green, dark large sans-serif English labels and generous whitespace. Landscape 1800x1100. Title: Robot learning: architecture and evidence. TOP panel heading Runtime control. Clean horizontal chain: Instruction + observations -> Semantic planner -> Skill and motion planning -> Nominal controller -> Constraint filter -> Robot. Small note beneath Semantic planner: Language grounding. Under Skill and motion planning: Feasibility checks. Under Constraint filter: Model + actuator assumptions. Draw feedback arrow from Robot to observations running below the chain, labeled State estimation + execution feedback. Constraint filter may be CLF/CBF and must have a clear branch downward labelled Infeasible -> Stop or fallback. Do not imply all semantic plans are safe or all CLF controllers collision-free. BOTTOM panel is clearly separate with heading Offline policy evaluation. A left input box Paired real + sim trials and another input box Additional sim trials both feed Bias correction, then Mean + confidence interval, then Review deployment evidence. A small note in this bottom panel reads Population statistics, not per-step guarantees. No arrows from the statistical confidence interval to motor torques or the runtime Constraint filter. Keep the two panels distinct. No success rate, benchmark, certification seal, robot medical claim or numeric performance statistic. Every label must be readable and all arrows unambiguous. Provide clear conceptual blocks, not dense equations.
review: Verified nominal control and constraint filtering remain conditional on modeling and actuator assumptions. Infeasibility branches to fallback. Offline paired simulation statistics are kept separate from runtime control; no per-step certificate is claimed from a confidence interval.
